sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Biocompatible Dental Ceramic Blocks and Milling Discs

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Luxembourg and the Federal Republic of Germany
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Luxembourg and the French Republic
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Luxembourg and the United States of America
Investment Protection Agreement between the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union and the Republic of Singapore

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the beneficial owner register (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant institution du registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on the beneficial owner register (Règlement grand-ducal du 13 janvier 2019 relatif au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the trade and companies register or equivalent certificate of good standing of a corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the country of incorporation of the partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if signatory) or Consular Legalization (if non-apostille country)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport (photo page) of each natural person partner and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notarial authority in the country of residence of the person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill) of each natural person partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or utility provider, with notarial certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residency certificate of each partner relevant to Luxembourg due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the partner's residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds declaration for each contributing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Partner's financial institution and signing partner under notarial or sworn oath

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All partners, prospective UBOs, and transactional counterparties must be screened against: (a) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, (b) UN Security Council consolidated list, (c) Luxembourg national freezing list maintained by the Ministry of Finance, (d) OFAC/SDN list and FATF high-risk jurisdictions list, (e) adverse media and PEP databases. Screening is conducted pre-onboarding, updated at least annually, and on any trigger event; PEP status, family members, and known associates are subject to enhanced due diligence per CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended and the amended Law of 12 November 2004. Detected matches must be reported to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic filing portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must comply with Article 20-1 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002. It must be written in Latin characters; if the name is in a non-Latin script, an official transliteration into the Latin alphabet must be provided. The name must be linguistically neutral or in French/German. It must not infringe on public policy or good morals. It must include a distinct legal form designation, i.e. 'Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)' or 'SCSp' as an indication of Limited Liability.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of rejection of the chosen name, the applicant is entitled to submit a written objection to the Registrar within one month. If the Registrar confirms the rejection, the applicant may bring an appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (District Court) in accordance with Article 21 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002. The appeal must be filed by a Luxembourg-licensed attorney and accompanied by the original rejection notice. A new name may be simultaneously reserved to avoid delay. If a reservation is active, it remains valid for 30 days; an extension of the reservation is not explicitly provided by statute, and a renewed reservation must be filed if incorporation is not completed within the window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual/registered agent offices are acceptable solely as a legal (statutory) registered office for a non-operational SCSp; however, for an entrepreneurial commercial operation in the manufacture of dental ceramic blocks and milling discs, the SCSp must maintain a physical operational establishment in Luxembourg if production occurs there. A pure letterbox arrangement without employees, assets, or physical activity will not satisfy Luxembourg tax residency or substance expectations and may be challenged under combatting tax avoidance guidelines (CbCR, ATAD).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High (approx. 65% per fiscal year) for a company engaged in regulated medical device/dental product manufacturing due to Health Inspectorate and authoritative laboratory audits; even for a passive holding SCSp, tax authorities may conduct physical checks (approx. 20%).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg legal counsel for SCSp partnership agreement drafting and pre-incorporation due diligence
Name availability search and reservation / preliminary clearance via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
Filing of the SCSp incorporation instrument (private deed or notarized deed) with the RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff (approx. €80 + agent handling fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the notice of incorporation in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff per line entry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of beneficial owners (RBE) and UBO piercing documentation review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RBE filing is free; service fee for UBO analysis and documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille and/or consular legalization of corporate and identity documents of non-resident partners (assuming 3 partners x 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaries and foreign ministries/consulates in the partners' residence jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or flat administrative fee per document plus courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory PEP, sanctions (EU/UN/OFAC/FATF), and adverse media screening on all partners and UBOs
Certified translation of KYC documents and corporate instruments into French/German where required

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 101-1 to 101-14 (SCSp regime inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013), and the Law of 12 July 2013 on the Special Limited Partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Deed and Articles of Association (Contrat de Société / Acte constitutif) filed via the LBR e-file portal with publication extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital requirement for an SCSp; contributions are freely determined in the partnership deed and may be made in cash, kind, or industry. Cash contributions should be held in a Luxembourg bank account, optionally escrowed, pending RCS registration and first drawdown for the dental ceramics manufacturing plant.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the partnership deed establishing the Société en Commandite Spéciale for the manufacture of biocompatible dental ceramic blocks and CAD/CAM milling discs is hereby approved, and the contributions subscribed by the General Partner and each Limited Partner, per the annexed schedule, are accepted in full. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the Manager is authorized to complete RCS registration and RESA publication. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole signatory authority over the operating and escrow accounts and full power to execute regulatory filings, hire counsel, and perfect all establishment and environmental licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the SCSp Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) if real property is contributed; otherwise a private deed executed by all partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp deed including corporate name, registered office address, duration, corporate object (ISIC 3250 manufactures of dental ceramic zirconia blocks/discs), contribution schedule per partner, profit and loss allocation, management powers, and bank signatory rules. Execute before a notary only where real estate or regulated assets are contributed; otherwise sign by private deed. Ensure the deed expressly designates the General Partner and the Manager (Gérant) and identifies the registered office physical address in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copies, proof of address, and source-of-funds statements for all partners
Certificate of corporate existence and RCS extract for any corporate partner or general partner
Draft partnership deed and contribution schedule
Consent of the registered office provider/landlord
Declaration of acceptance of office by the Manager (Gérant)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is challenged for lack of notarization despite a real estate contribution, re-execute the deed notarially and re-file; any partner objection is resolved by deed amendment subject to unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the SCSp with the RCS via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Luxembourg (Luxembourg Business Registers, LBR e-file portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership deed and the standardized RCS filing form electronically through the LBR e-file system. Provide the required identification data for managers, registered office, and the corporate object. Pay the electronic filing fee online and await the RCS certificate of registration and the allocation of the Luxembourg business registration number.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership deed (PDF, certified if requested)
LBR filing form (formulaire RCS) duly completed
Identity documents and proof of address of managers (less than 3 months old)
Domiciliation consent and registered office address proof
Manager acceptance declaration and specimen signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any RCS query within 30 calendar days via the LBR e-file inbox; correct incomplete entries or missing exhibits and resubmit. If registration is refused, rectify the deed with a supplementary deed and re-file; legal review by Luxembourg counsel is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Corporate Acts in the RESA Electronic Compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful RCS registration, the registry automatically generates an extract for publication in RESA, as mandated by the Law of 10 August 1915. Verify the published notice within one month of the deed date; retain the official publication certificate as evidence of third-party effectiveness.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RESA publication proof (justificatif de publication)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or defective, file a request for correction with the RCS and, if necessary, apply to the competent district court for an order to rectify the published extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Luxembourg Fiscal Matriculation Number and VAT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and the National Identification Register (Registre National).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic registration forms (including VAT registration) with the AEDT, attaching the RCS extract and partnership deed. Disclose the industrial activity as ISIC 3250/NACE 32.50 (manufacture of dental instruments and supplies) and describe the planned manufacturing operations. Obtain the Luxembourg matriculation number (numéro de matricule) and, where required, the VAT number for intra-community trade and invoicing.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
Certified copy of the partnership deed
AEDT registration forms and VAT questionnaire
Identification of the Manager (Gérant)
Projected annual turnover and activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests clarification on the taxable status or activity classification, file an amended return and supporting market analysis; obtain a formal VAT ruling where cross-border dental supplies may qualify for reduced or exempt treatment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration with the Social Security Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) and the Accident Insurance Association (AAA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS upon hiring staff, submitting the statutory registration form and the partnership deed. Appoint a responsible person for social declarations; activate electronic declaration channels (e-CSS) for monthly payroll reporting. Ensure accident insurance cover through the Association d'assurance accident and worker health monitoring through the approved occupational health service.
required_dossiers: CCSS employer registration form
RCS extract and partnership deed
List of future employees and payroll start date
Identity documents of the employer representative
Occupational health service mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS delays the employer number, escalate to the CCSS front office with proof of RCS and AEDT registration; retroactive declarations on the effective hire date are permitted once the employer number is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Establishment Authorization, Environmental Notification, and Local Civil Defense Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (Direction générale des classes moyennes); Administration de l'environnement; Commune / municipal authorities; Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the business establishment authorization application under the amended Law of 8 February 2017, demonstrating professional capacity (diploma or professional experience) and good repute. Simultaneously submit the environmental notification for the classified installation (établissement classé) under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 for the zirconia sintering, milling, and dust-extraction plant. Coordinate with the commune and CGDIS for fire safety inspection and with the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) for occupational safety approval before machinery startup.
required_dossiers: Establishment authorization application form and business plan
Diplomas, professional certificates, or 3,000 hours of professional experience evidence
Criminal record certificate (certificat de non-faillite) and good repute proof
Classified installation notification form and environmental checklist
Site plan, structural stability certificate, and electrical conformity certificate
CGDIS fire safety assessment and ITM work-safety dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authorization is queried, supplement the dossier with additional professional or technical evidence within the statutory deadline; if refused, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification and, where applicable, request an additional public inquiry for the environmental permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale des classes moyennes (establishment authorization) in coordination with the Ministère de la Santé, Direction de la Santé, Division Pharmacie et Médicaments (medical device manufacturer economic operator registration under Regulation (EU) 2017/745).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Authorization (Autorisation d'établissement) and Manufacturer / Economic Operator Registration for Class I medical devices (dental CAD/CAM zirconia blocks) under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, together with the Classified Establishment Running Permit (Autorisation ou notification d'établissement classé) under the amended Law of 10 June 1999.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 (notification) under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments; the small-capacity zirconia ceramic sintering and milling plant falls below the mandatory full EIA thresholds of the Law of 15 May 2018, but requires a screening notice and environmental impact assessment statement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges into municipal sewerage must meet the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 November 2009 limits (suspended matter, pH, heavy metals); airborne particulates and VOCs from sintering furnaces must comply with the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU as transposed by the Law of 9 May 2022; solid zirconia milling residues and contaminated abrasives must be managed under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, with recycling or approved waste carrier disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) covering the furnace room, compressed gases, and powder storage; workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) including machine guarding, local exhaust ventilation for zirconia dust, personal protective equipment protocol, and noise assessment; structural load inspection certificate for the milling and sintering equipment by an approved engineer; electrical installation conformity certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV) for VAT and indirect taxes; online portal: myguichet.lu and guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp, the entity first obtains legal existence and a national registration number (matricule national) by filing its articles of association and managerial information with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR). After RCS registration, the SCSp files VAT Form 640 (registration as taxable person) with the AEDTV through MyGuichet or by paper, attaching the RCS excerpt, partnership agreement, proof of registered office in Luxembourg, identification of all partners and the manager (whether a resident individual or corporate entity), and a description of the taxable activity. The AEDTV issues a VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits). For corporate income tax, the SCSp itself is fiscally transparent; however, the competent director opens a tax file on the partnership for reporting purposes and to allocate income to partners under their respective residence tax authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The SCSp is a contractual partnership that is fiscally transparent for corporate income tax and net wealth tax; it is not a separate taxable person. Each partner is individually taxed on its share of the partnership's income in accordance with Luxembourg law. For VAT purposes, the SCSp is treated as a separate taxable person where it carries out an economic activity in its own name. The registered office and place of effective management in Luxembourg determine territorial fiscal presence, but because the SCSp is transparent, direct tax exposure arises at the partner level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a 'check-the-box' election comparable to the United States. The SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent; the partnership agreement cannot elect to convert the vehicle into a corporation for local tax purposes. Within the transparent framework, the partners may contractually allocate profits, losses, and distributions, and may elect to apply the provisions of the Luxembourg law implementing ATAD and hybrid mismatch rules. For VAT, an SCSp may voluntarily register for VAT upon conducting a taxable activity and may elect the small-business exemption conditions where annual turnover is below the statutory threshold; no analogous election exists for income tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Luxembourg Value Added Tax - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold applies: a Luxembourg-established SCSp is required to register for VAT from the first taxable transaction. A small-business franchise exemption may be claimed where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 15,000 (subject to statutory conditions and general exclusion for services and supplies that are exempted or non-established).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping for private B2B transactions. E-invoicing in a structured electronic format (EN 16931 in the PEPPOL network) is mandatory only for B2G public procurement via the Luxembourg public e-invoicing portal (myguichet / JOS). For all other B2B and export transactions, VAT invoices must meet EU standard invoicing requirements (VAT number, date, supply description, amount, VAT rate) and may be issued on paper or in electronic form provided authenticity of origin and integrity are ensured. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposals will progressively extend e-invoicing requirements to B2B supplies, but these are not yet in force in Luxembourg.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies to supplies of dental zirconia ceramic blocks physically dispatched from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods leave EU customs territory within the statutory deadline (normally 90 days but subject to the customs declaration and exit confirmation) and valid proof of export is retained. Intra-EU dispatch to a VAT-registered customer in another Member State is eligible for zero-rating under Article 41 of the VAT law where the customer's VAT identification number and an EC sales list are reported. Services physically and effectively performed for customers outside the EU fall outside Luxembourg VAT in accordance with place-of-supply rules, but the SCSp must substantiate the non-EU status of the recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document submitted via the Luxembourg customs AES/‘Le Déclaration Électronique’ system) producing a Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Proof of Exit — exit summary declaration, customs transit document (T1), or border endorsement evidencing that the goods left the EU
Bill of Lading, combined transport bill, or air waybill issued in the name of the Luxembourg exporter
Commercial invoice stated as 'Export — 0% VAT' with reference to the underlying sales contract
Inward remittance certificate, bank transfer confirmation, or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a foreign currency or credited to the exporter's account
Packing list and transport booking/CIM/CMR documentation evidencing dispatch to the non-EU buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the VAT administration determines that an export zero-rating claim was unsupported, false, or not substantiated by adequate transport and exit evidence, the supply is recharacterised as a taxable domestic supply. The VAT due at 17% is then assessed de novo. Late-payment interest accrues at the annual statutory rate (currently approximately 3.6% p.a. or as adjusted), and administrative penalties apply per Article 33 of the VAT enforcement law: up to 20% for material omissions or accurate-return defects, up to 50% for concealed or unauthorised deductions, and amounts up to 100% of the VAT evaded for fraudulent conduct or bad faith. Criminal sanctions are available under the General Tax Code for intentional VAT fraud, including fines and imprisonment. The statutory limitation for issuing a VAT assessment is generally five years from the end of the filing year, extended to ten years for fraudulent or deliberately concealed situations. Export documents must be retained and made available upon request within the assessment window; the 180-day substantive deadline is applied as a practical documentary proof convention and does not dissolve the longer statutory clawback risk.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem; financial supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banks, payment institutions, and e-money institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full currency convertibility under EU Treaty capital and payments provisions. Both current and capital account transactions are freely permitted for residents and non-residents. Profit remittance from a Luxembourg SCSp is treated as a distributive payment to partners and may be made without exchange control approval, subject to CRS, FATCA, AML/KYC verification, and tax withholding review where applicable. No Luxembourg exchange control licence is required for inbound or outbound transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion timeline, or forced repatriation ratio for export receipts in Luxembourg. Exporters of dental zirconia blocks and other goods may retain foreign currency in bank accounts or receive EUR directly. Balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL may apply above set thresholds, but no conversion obligation exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium for SCSp capital subscriptions and escrow purposes; more viable for day-to-day operational FX conversion within the EEA. CSSF-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) with PSD2 passporting rights can open payment accounts and execute FX conversion for euro-denominated flows, but they cannot grant credit, hold notarial escrow balances, or perform the full banking functions expected for capital injection confirmation. Offshore digital EMIs without an EEA passport generally cannot lawfully provide payment services to Luxembourg entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Luxembourg SCSp, the general partner's authorised manager or signatory will generally be required to appear physically for first account opening, particularly where non-EU ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) are present. CSSF-compliant remote video KYC may be accepted by some banks, but original corporate documents, apostilled powers of attorney, and notarised SCSp deeds must still be couriered. Remote onboarding is feasible only for straightforward structures with transparent EU-based ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO transparency action required for an SCSp with non-EU corporate investors or nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully completed Luxembourg UBO declaration (LVTaff), organisational chart identifying natural persons owning more than 25%, certificate of incorporation, notarised SCSp limited partnership agreement, certified passport copies, register of beneficial owners extract, and a legal opinion explaining the pass-through nature of the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds alert for capital contribution exceeding EUR 100,000
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor bank statements covering at least 12 months, audited financial statements or tax records of contributing entities, source of wealth statement executed by the principal, confirmation letters from foreign banks, and a capital contribution declaration signed by the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening mismatch arising from trade counterparties or supplier list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full contract file for dental zirconia trade transactions, commercial invoices, shipping documents, end-user declarations, sanctions screening reports, and an independent compliance opinion confirming no restricted jurisdiction or prohibited counterparty involvement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 for non-euro currencies or SEPA credit transfer for euro funding. The sending bank should use payment narrative 'Subscription to Luxembourg SCSp capital account' and include the SCSp name, general partner reference, and purpose of payment. Verification is provided through the bank's account confirmation, notarised capital subscription statement, and the Luxembourg register filing; no prior BCL exchange control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should use SWIFT MT103 for direct TT payments to suppliers of zirconia powder, milling blanks, and laboratory equipment. For larger recurring shipments, a documentary commercial letter of credit under UCP600 with a confirming bank is the recommended clearing rail, using MT700/MT710 messages. Payment release is exercised against compliant trade documents (invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts executed with CSSF-regulated credit institutions
FX swaps for managing near-term euro/foreign currency liquidity positions
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term financing liability hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies subject to offshore convertibility restrictions, provided underlying trade exposure is documented and EMIR reporting obligations are observed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS Annual Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des inscriptions au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of the following calendar year (first-quarter filing window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 250 per late submission; persistent non-filing for more than 24 months triggers ex officio strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, or within one month of any change in beneficial ownership, whichever is earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal sanctions: 8 days to 1 year imprisonment and EUR 10,000–100,000 fine for deliberate non-disclosure; administrative strike-off after repeated non-confirmation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) — applicable only when the SCSp is not exempt under partnership/small-undertaking rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RCS (electronic filing via eRCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year end; for a calendar year-end, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial court late-filing fine up to EUR 2,000; continued failure may lead to court-ordered dissolution and criminal fine for the manager.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Tax Information Return (déclaration fiscale annuelle d'une société de personnes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the following tax year; electronic filers under e-TVA may receive extension to 31 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of assessed tax (minimum EUR 75), default interest at 0.6% per month, and possible ex officio assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory statutory audit applies to an SCSp that exceeds two of the three Luxembourg size thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average headcount 50 employees. An audit may also be mandated by the articles of association or if partners holding at least 10% of capital request one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and annual accounts, as amended) for individual statutory accounts; consolidated accounts, if applicable, follow IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every transfer of partnership interests must be reported to the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month. The annual confirmation shall validate that the recorded UBO data are accurate and complete as of the confirmation date, even when no changes occurred. The confirmation is filed electronically, signed by a Luxembourg-resident manager or authorised agent, and does not require a government fee.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partnership Interest Transfers and UBO History
Register of Managers and Statutory Auditors

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% standard Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT) rate for taxable profits exceeding EUR 175,000; 15% up to EUR 175,000; plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax. An LU SCSp is a fiscally transparent partnership and is not itself subject to CIT; taxable profit is allocated to partners and taxed in their hands.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; relevant preferences are the Luxembourg IP box (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective headline below 5%), participation exemption for qualifying dividends/capital gains, and notional interest deduction (NID). For a transparent SCSp, these incentives apply at the level of the taxable partners where the underlying conditions are satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 563 – Déclaration pour l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités (Luxembourg CIT/income tax return); transmitted electronically via the Luxembourg authorities’ eCDF portal (MyGuichet.lu). A tax-transparent SCSp does not file a standalone CIT return, but a corporate partner subject to CIT includes its SCSp profit share in its own Form 563.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Balance-sheet date + 5 months (generally 31 May of the following year); professional tax representatives may obtain an administrative extension, commonly to 31 December or later.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result of the SCSp or corporate partner, reconciled to audited commercial accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner does not file this box unless it carries on a Luxembourg permanent establishment; enter the PE-share attributable to the Luxembourg activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses, including production costs, depreciation, R&D and service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically connected with the Luxembourg PE or with the partner’s taxable Luxembourg-source income are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items, hidden profit distributions, taxes and other add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must add back items that are non-deductible under Luxembourg rules even if deductible in the home country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward claimed in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transparent SCSp losses are allocated annually to partners; the partner claims loss relief under its own tax rules and with applicable anti-abuse limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying IP income deduction (80% exemption) and notional interest deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim requires a Luxembourg economic-substance/use assessment at partner level; supporting documentation must be contemporaneous.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Répartition du résultat entre associés
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership profit/loss allocation schedule to general and limited partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners with no Luxembourg PE generally have limited or no Luxembourg tax exposure; residence certificate is necessary if treaty protection is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Representative declaration, email and reference to the tax adviser.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with a Luxembourg filing obligation must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative with power of attorney if so required by the ACD.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may lead to a default assessment; late-filing penalty up to 10% of the tax due and late-payment interest at 0.80% per month (9.60% p.a.). Fraudulent omission carries criminal penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by a resident fully taxable company. A transparent SCSp distribution is not a dividend for Luxembourg WHT purposes; the partners are taxed directly. If the SCSp opts/ is treated as a taxable corporation, a subsequent distribution to partners may be subject to 15% WHT, with treaty relief where available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduction or exemption, the beneficial-owner partner must file Luxembourg withholding-tax relief forms (Form 502/503 series) with the Administration des Contributions Directes before payment, attaching a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the residence jurisdiction and, where relevant, proof of holding period/share percentage. If tax was withheld and no pre-clearance was obtained, the partner may claim refund by submitting a DTA refund request to the ACD within the relevant statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties by a Luxembourg borrower/licensee is generally 0%. Under Luxembourg’s DTA network, interest may be taxable at 0/5/10% and royalties at 0/5%; the applicable treaty rate depends on the specific DTA and beneficial-ownership requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg CbC reporting threshold: consolidated group revenue of EUR 750,000,000. Master File/Local File contemporaneous documentation is required when related-party transactions exceed EUR 500,000 in aggregate (administrative practice); the ACD may also require documentation for any quantum under Article 56bis L.I.R.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style ESR statute, but substance is the touchstone of Luxembourg anti-abuse, treaty-benefit, IP-regime and ATAD GAAR analysis. An SCSp holding/operating intellectual property, invoicing dental blocks, or booking intercompany services must show real decision-making, qualified staff, operational premises, appropriate expenditure, and economic risk in Luxembourg; a letterbox SCSp is exposed to recharacterization at partner level.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing profit allocations, omitting taxable sales of zirconia blocks, using fabricated invoices or artificial intermediary companies to divert Luxembourg-source profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax assessments, 0.80% monthly late-payment interest, criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for up to five years. The SCSp’s tax advantages are voided retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/managers of the general partner may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes and civil restitution; travel bans and imprisonment can be imposed in aggravated fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file, late filing and non-cooperation with ACD
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing annual tax returns, refusing to file TP documentation, disregarding information orders or obstructing the Luxembourg tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Default tax assessment for the SCSp/partners; late-filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax; monthly late-payment interest; administrative fines for defective filing; possible publication of tax-default facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner’s directors can be held personally liable for penalties if the default results from their wilful misconduct or gross negligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / abusive treaty shopping / GAAR (ATAD)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The dental-CAD/CAM SCSp has no physical office, no full-time employees, no board/partner decision-making records in Luxembourg, yet claims treaty benefits, Parent-Subsidiary exemption or IP box relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of exemption/deduction, recharacterization as taxable dividend/royalty/interest, additional tax and interest, potential exit-tax adjustments on migrated IP. Cross-border arrangements may be targeted by the ACD and foreign anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign artificial tax shelter documents may face civil liability for the lost tax, fines and travel restrictions under criminal tax-fraud procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation failure and non-arm’s length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dental zirconia blocks/discs to related distributors at non-arm’s-length prices; inadequate Local File; relying on group-wide formulary allocations not accepted by Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer-pricing adjustment, secondary adjustments on deemed dividends, penalties up to 5% of the cross-border adjustment, and interest. No Luxembourg safe harbor protects excessive intercompany margins without functional/substance analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may be asserted against directors who approved intentionally mispriced related-party contracts or destroyed contemporaneous evidence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SCSp’s ultimate beneficial owners are undisclosed, or the partnership is used to move proceeds through SWIFT/TT channels without AML/KYC checks, contrary to Luxembourg AML legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under Luxembourg AML laws, including fines of up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons and imprisonment for natural persons; administrative proceedings may suspend partnership activities and deregister the SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner can be named in AML investigations, blocked from travel, fined personally and subject to imprisonment where laundering is proved.
